scope: Ordinary single- and double-card SLT logic in the completed source and manual supply-pin review; connectors, resistor terminators, switches and other nonstandard modules excluded.
direct_human_statement: I believe we have no unexplained use of power pins in ALD diagrams anymore, correct? They are used to tie otherwise undriven nets or inputs to ground or to +3V, and the one exception is the limiter block which is to make the connection to the transformer ground.
conclusion: No unexplained power-contact use remains in the reviewed ordinary SLT logic scope. Remaining genuine contacts tie otherwise undriven nets/inputs to ground or +3V. KD901 AS (S21AA / 3310A1) D08 is the transformer-ground reference for its mains-frequency limiter.
negative_and_six_volt_conclusion: No unexplained -3V or +6V contact use remains in the reviewed ordinary logic cases.
annotation_caveat: Literal numeric pin/wire annotations are preserved. The meaning of 8 is unresolved; L-as-latch is a human hypothesis. These annotation questions are separate from the identified supply connection.
current_release: Supply pin visual and human current audit.json
